title: Shang-Chi writer confirms work on sequel
excerpt:
Dave Callaham confirms he is working on a Shang-Chi sequel.
The project is in early development without a release date.
body_md:
Five years after the release of Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, screenwriter Dave Callaham has confirmed that he is working on a sequel to the Marvel Studios film. Speaking on the Escape Hatch podcast, the writer described the project as being in its early stages while indicating that meaningful progress is taking place.

Callaham's comments provide a more concrete indication of development than general expressions of interest in another standalone Shang-Chi adventure. Although the actor Simu Liu has previously discussed the character's future, the writer's confirmation establishes that work on a follow-up is actively occupying his attention.

That development should not be confused with confirmation of a production schedule. Marvel has not announced an official sequel title, filming start date or theatrical release date in the available report. Early screenwriting work is an important step for a potential feature, but considerable development may still be required before the film is ready to enter production.

Released in 2021, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings introduced Liu as the title character in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. During the interview, Callaham also reflected positively on the decision to cast Liu, emphasizing the combination of acting experience, comedic timing and physical abilities that made him particularly suitable for the role. The actor's background in taekwondo and parkour contributed to that combination.

Audiences are also expected to see Liu return as Shang-Chi in Avengers: Doomsday, which is scheduled for theatrical release on December 18, 2026. His involvement in the crossover creates an opportunity for Marvel to explore the character's place within its wider superhero ensemble before a possible return to standalone storytelling.

The events of Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars could influence the direction of the sequel, but the available report does not confirm its chronological setting or how directly it will connect with either crossover. Those possibilities remain distinct from the confirmed news of Callaham's involvement.

Several narrative threads from the original film also remain relevant to discussions about a follow-up. Shang-Chi and Katy's encounter with Wong suggested further adventures, while Xialing's assumption of leadership over the Ten Rings organization established another potential source of future conflict and character development.

Whether the new screenplay will focus on those elements or introduce an entirely different storyline is not yet known. For now, Callaham's confirmation represents an encouraging development for viewers who have been waiting for Shang-Chi to headline another film, without establishing details that Marvel has not officially announced.
